chapters: And it was after the death of Yehoshua, that the children of Yisroel asked of Havayah, saying, "Who shall go up for us first against the Kena'anim, to fight against them?"
And Havayah said, Yehudah shall go up; behold I have given the land into his hand.
And Yehudah said to Shimon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and we will fight against the Kena'anim, and I will also go with you into your lot." And Shimon went with him.
And Yehudah went up; and Havayah gave the Kena'anim and the Perizim into their hands; and they smote them in Bezek, ten thousand men.
And they found Adoni- bezek in Bezek and fought with him: and they smote the Kena'anim and the Perizim.
And Adoni-Bezek fled, and they pursued him: and they caught him and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.

And Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered under my table; as I have done, so has Elokim punished me." And they brought him to Yerushalayim, and he died there.
And the children of Yehudah fought against Yerushalayim and captured it, and smote it with the edge of the sword; and set the city on fire.
And afterward the children of Yehudah went down to fight against the Kena'anim; the inhabitants of the mountains, of the South, and of the lowland.
And Yehudah went to the Kena'anim that dwelt in Chevron-Now the name of Chevron formerly had been Kiryat-arba-and they smote Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.
And from there he went to the inhabitants of Devir-Now the name of Devir formerly had been Kiryat-Sefer.
And Kalev said, "He that shall smite Kiryat-Sefer and capture it; to him will I give Achsah my daughter for a wife."
And Otniel the son of Kenaz, Kalev's younger brother, captured it; and he gave him Achsah his daughter for a wife.
And it was when she came to him, that she persuaded him to ask of her father the field, and she leaned off the donkey. And Kalev said to her, "What is to you?"
And she said to him, "Give me a blessing, for you have given me dry land; and you should give me springs of water." And Kalev gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

And the children of Keni, the father-in-law of Moshe, went up from the city of date palms, with the children of Yehudah into the wilderness of Yehudah, which is south of Arad; and he went and dwelt with the people.
And Yehudah went with Shimon his brother, and they smote the Kena'anim that inhabited Tzefat; and they destroyed it, and called the name of the city, Chormah.
And Yehudah captured Azah with its territory, and Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
And Havayah was with Yehudah, and they drove out the inhabitants of the mountains; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, for they had iron chariots.
And they gave Chevron to Kalev, as Moshe had spoken; and he drove out from there the three sons of the giant.
And the children of Binyamin did not drive out the Yevusim that inhabited Yerushalayim; and the Yevusim dwelt with the children of Binyamin in Yerushalayim until this day.
And the house of Yosef, they also went up to Beit-El; and Havayah was with them.
And the house of Yosef caused to spy Beit-El. Now the name of the city formerly was Luz.
And the watchers saw a man leave the city. And they said to him, "Show us now the entrance to the city and we will deal kindly with you."
And he showed them the entrance of the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but the man and his entire family they let go.
And the man went to the land of the Chittim, and built a city, and called its name Luz; this is its name until this day.

And Menasheh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beit-She'an and its towns, Ta'anach and its towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, the inhabitants of Yibleam and its towns, the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; and the Kena'anim wanted to remain in this land.
And it was when Yisroel became strong, that they put the Kena'anim to tribute, but they did not drive them out.
And Efraim did not drive out the Kena'anim that dwelt in Gezer; and the Kena'anim dwelt among them in Gezer.
Zevulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; and the Kena'anim dwelt among them and became tributary.
Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Akko, nor the inhabitants of Tzidon, nor of Achlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Chelbah, nor of Afik, nor of Rechob.
And the Asherim dwelt among the Kena'anim, the inhabitants of the land; for they did not drive them out.

Naftali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beit-Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beit-Anat; and he dwelt among the Kena'anim, the inhabitants of the land. And the inhabitants of Beit-Shemesh and of Beit-Anat became tributary to them.
And the Emorim forced the children of Dan to the mountain; for they would not let them come down to the valley.
And the Emorim wanted to remain on Mount Cheres, in Ayalon, and in Sha'alvim; but the hand of the house of Yosef prevailed and they became tributary.
And the border of the Emorim was from Ma'aleh-Akrabim, from the rock upward.

And a messenger of Havayah went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I will take you up from Mitzrayim and I have brought you to the land that I have sworn to your forefathers and I said, 'I will not break my covenant with you forever.
And you shall not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land, their altars you shall smash,' but you have not obeyed Me, what have you done?
And I also said, 'I will not drive them out from before you, and they will be pokers to you and their deities will be a stumbling block to you.' "
And it was while the messenger of Havayah was saying these words to all the children of Yisroel, that the nation raised their voices and cried.
And they called the name of that place Bochim and they sacrificed to Havayah there.
And Yehoshua had sent away the nation, and the children of Yisroel went, each man to his inheritance to possess the land.
And the nation served Havayah during all the days of Yehoshua and all the days of the elders that outlived Yehoshua and who had seen all the great deed of Havayah that He had performed for Yisroel.
And Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of Havayah, died, being one hundred and ten years old.
And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnah Cheres on the mountain of Efraim, to the north of Mount Gaash.
And also all that generation were gathered to their forefathers, and there arose another generation after them, who knew not Havayah nor the deed which He had done for Yisroel.
And the children of Yisroel did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah and they served the Be'alim.

And they forsook Elokim of their forefathers, Who had brought them up from the land of Mitzrayim, and they went after other deities, of the deities of the nations that were around them, and they bowed to them and they provoked Havayah.
And they forsook Havayah and served the Baal and the Ashtarot.

And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Yisroel, and He delivered them into the hands of spoilers and they spoiled them, and He gave them over into the hands of their enemies around, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.
Wherever they went out, the hand of Havayah was against them for evil, as Havayah had spoken and as Havayah had sworn to them, and they were greatly distressed.
And Havayah raised up judges and they saved them from the hands of those who had spoiled them.

But also their judges they did not obey, for they went astray after other deities, and they bowed to them; they turned aside quickly from the way wherein their forefathers had walked, obeying the commandments of Havayah, they did not do so.

And when Havayah raised them up judges, then Havayah was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge, for Havayah retracted, because of their cry by reason of them that oppressed them and crushed them.

And it was when the judge died, that they would return and deal more corruptly than their forefathers, going after other deities to serve them and to bow down to them; they did not diminish of their practices nor of their stubborn way.
And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Yisroel and He said, "Because this nation has transgressed my covenant which I commanded their forefathers and have not obeyed Me,
I too will not continue to drive out any man from before them, of the nations that Yehoshua left and he died.
In order to test Yisroel through them, whether they would keep the way of Havayah to walk therein as their forefathers did keep it, or not."
And Havayah left these nations without driving them out hastily, and He did not give them into the hand of Yehoshua.
Now these are the nations which Havayah left through whom to test Yisroel, all those that had not known all the wars of Kena'an.
Only that the generations of the children of Yisroel should know, to teach them war, just the earlier ones did not know thereof.
The five lords of the Pelishtim, and all the Kena'anim, and the Tzidonim, and the Chivim that dwelt in Mount Levanon, from Mount Baal-Chermon to the passageway of Chamat.
And they were to test through them Yisroel, to know whether they would obey the commandments of Havayah which He had commanded their forefathers through Moshe.
And the children of Yisroel dwelt among the Kena'anim, the Chittim, and the Emorim, and the Perizim, and the Chivim, and the Yevusim.
And they took their daughters to themselves for wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and served their deities.
And the children of Yisroel did that which displeased Havayah, and they forgot Havayah their Elokim, and served the Be'alim and the Asherot.

And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Yisroel, and He gave them over into the hands of Kushan-Rishatayim, king of Aram-Naharayim; and the children of Yisroel served Kushan-Rishatayim eight years.
And the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah, and Havayah raised up a savior to the children of Yisroel who saved them; Otniel the son of Kenaz, Kalev's brother, who was younger than he.

And the spirit of Havayah came upon him, and he judged Yisroel; and he went out to war, and Havayah delivered into his hands Kushan-Rishatayim the king of Aram; and his hand prevailed upon Kushan-Rishatayim.
And the land had rest forty years; then Otniel the son of Kenaz died.
And the children of Yisroel continued to do that which displeased Havayah; and Havayah strengthened Eglon the king of Moav against Yisroel, because they had done that which displeased Havayah.
And he gathered to him the children of Amon and Amalek; and he went and smote Yisroel, and they possessed the city of the date palms.
And the children of Yisroel served Eglon the king of Moav eighteen years.

And the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah, and Havayah raised up for them a savior, Ehud the son of Gera, the Binyamini, a man with a shriveled right hand; and the children of Yisroel sent through him a present to Eglon the king of Moav.
And Ehud made for himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit was its length; and he girded it under his clothing on his right thigh.
And he offered the present to Eglon king of Moav.
And it was when he had finished offering the present, that he escorted the people who had carried the present.
And he turned back from the quarries that were by Gilgal and said, "I have a secret errand with you O King." And he said, "Be quiet," and all that stood near him went out.
And Ehud came to him, and he was sitting by himself in the cool upper room which he had for himself, and Ehud said, "I have a message from Elokim to you," and he stood up from the chair.
And Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.
And the haft also went in after the blade, and the fat closed upon the blade, because he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the excrement came out.
And Ehud went out to the porch and shut the doors of the upper room in front of him, and locked them.
Now when he had gone out, his servants came and saw, and behold, the doors of the upper room were locked; and they said, "Surely he is covering his feet in the cool room."
And they tarried until it was late, and behold, he did not open the doors of the upper room; and they took the key and opened them, and behold their master was fallen down on the earth, dead.
And Ehud escaped while they lingered; and he passed beyond the quarries and escaped to Seirah.
And it was when he came, that he blew the trumpet on the mountain of Efraim; and the children of Yisroel went down with him from the mountain, and he was before them.

And he said to them, "Follow me quickly, for Havayah has given your enemies, the Moavim, into your hands." And they went down after him and seized the fords of the Yarden to Moav, and did not permit any man to pass.
And they killed of Moav at that time about ten thousand men, every lusty and every man of valor; and no man escaped.
And Moav was subdued on that day under the hand of Yisroel. And the land had rest eighty years.
And after him was Shamgar the son of Anat, and he killed the Pelishtim six hundred men with an ox-goad; and he also saved Yisroel.
And the children of Yisroel continued to do that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah, and Ehud was dead.
And Havayah gave them over into the hand of Yabin, the king of Kena'an, who reigned in Chatzor; and the chieftain of his army was Sisera, and he dwelt in Charoshet-Goyim.
And the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah; for he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed the children of Yisroel mightily for twenty years.
Now Devorah was a woman prophetess, the wife of Lapidot; she judged Yisroel at that time.
And she sat under the palm tree of Devorah, between Ramah and Beit-El, in the mountain of Efraim; and the children of Yisroel came up to her for judgment.

And she sent and called Barak the son of Avinoam out of Kedesh-Naftali. And she said to him, "Indeed Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, commanded, 'Go and draw toward Mount Tavor, and take with you ten thousand men of the children of Naftali and of the children of Zevulun.
And I shall draw to you, to the brook Kishon, Sisera, the chieftain of Yabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will give him into your hand.' "
And Barak said to her, "If you will go with me then I shall go, but if you will not go with me, I shall not go."

And she said, "I shall surely go with you, but your glory will not be on the way which you go, for into the hand of a woman will Havayah deliver Sisera." And Devorah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak gathered Zevulun and Naftali to Kedesh; and ten thousand men went up at his feet; and Devorah went up with him.
Now Chever the Keini had separated from the Keinim, of the children of Hobab the father-in-law of Moshe; and he pitched his tent as far as Elon-Beitzaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
And they told Sisera that Barak, the son of Avinoam, had gone up to Mount Tavor.
And Sisera gathered all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people that were with him, from Charoshet-Goyim, to the brook Kishon.

And Devorah said to Barak, "Rise, for this is the day which Havayah has given Sisera into your hand. Did not Havayah go out before you?" And Barak went down from Mount Tavor, with ten thousand men after him.
And Havayah confused Sisera and all the chariots and all of the camp with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera alighted from his chariot, and fled on foot.
And Barak pursued the chariots and the camp, to Charoshet-Goyim; and all of Sisera's camp fell by the edge of the sword, not even one was left.
And Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Ya'el, the wife of Chever the Keini; for there was peace between Yabin the king of Chatzor and the house of Chever the Keini.
And Ya'el went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn in, my master, turn in to me; fear not." And he turned in to her into the tent, and she covered him with a garment.
And he said to her, "Give me now a little water to drink, for I am thirsty;" and she opened the flask of milk and gave him to drink, and covered him.
And he said to her, "Stand in the doorway of the tent; and it shall be, if any man comes and asks you and says, 'Is a man here?,' then you shall say, 'There is not.' "

And Ya'el, the wife of Chever, took the tent-pin, and placed the hammer in her hand, and came to him stealthily, and thrust the pin into his temple, and it pierced through into the ground; and he was in a deep sleep and weary; and he died.

And behold, Barak pursued Sisera, and Ya'el came out to meet him, and she said to him, "Come and I will show you the man whom you seek," and he came to her, and behold, Sisera lay dead, and the pin was in his temple.
And Elokim subdued on that day Yabin the king of Kena'an, before the children of Yisroel.
And the hand of the children of Yisroel prevailed constantly harder against Yabin the king of Kena'an, until they had destroyed Yabin, king of Kena'an.
Now Devorah and Barak the son of Avinoam sang on that day, saying.
"When breaches are made in Yisroel, when the people offer themselves willingly, bless Havayah.
Hear, O kings, give ear, O princes; I, to Havayah I shall sing, I shall sing to Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
Havayah, when You went forth out of Se'ir, when You marched out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens also dripped; also the clouds dripped water.
The mountains melted at the presence of Havayah, this Sinai, because of the presence of Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
In the days of Shamgar the son of Anat, in the days of Ya'el, caravans ceased, and travellers walked on crooked paths.
The open cities ceased, in Yisroel they ceased, until I Devorah arose; I arose as a mother in Yisroel.
When they chose new deities, then there was war in the cities; was there seen a shield or a spear forty thousand Yisroel?
My heart is toward the lawgivers of Yisroel, that offered themselves willingly among the people, 'Bless Havayah.'
The riders of white donkeys, those that sit in judgment, and those that walk on the path, tell of it.

Instead of the noise of adversaries, between the places of drawing water, there they will tell the righteous acts of Havayah, the righteous acts of restoring open cities in Yisroel. Then the people of Havayah went down to the cities.
Praise! Praise! Devorah. Praise! Praise! Utter a song. Arise Barak, and capture your captives, son of Avinoam.
Then ruled a remnant among the mighty of the nations; Havayah dominated the strong for me.
Out of Efraim, whose root was against Amalek; after you Binyamin with your abaters; out of Machir came down officers, and out of Zevulun they that handle the pen of the scribe.
And the princes of Yissachar were with Devorah, as was Yissachar with Barak; into the valley they rushed forth with their feet. Among the divisions of Reuven, great resolves of heart.
Why do you sit between the borders, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? At the divisions of Reuven, great searchings of heart.
Gilad abides beyond the Yarden; and Dan, why does he gather into the ships? Asher dwelt at the shore of the seas, and by his breaches he abides.
Zevulun is a people that jeopardized their lives to die, as did Naftali, upon the high places of the field.
The kings came and fought; then fought the kings of Kena'an in Ta'anach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money.
From heaven they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
The brook Kishon swept them away, that ancient brook, the brook Kishon; tread down, O my soul, strength.
Then were pounded the heels of the horses by reason of the prancings, the prancings of their mighty ones.
'Curse you Meroz,' said the messenger of Havayah, 'curse you bitterly inhabitants thereof,' because they came not to the aid of Havayah, to the aid of Havayah against the mighty.
Blessed above women shall Ya'el, the wife of Chever the Keini, be; above women in the tent shall she be blessed.
Water he requested, milk she gave him: in a lordly bowl she brought him cream.
She put forth her hand to the pin, and her right hand to strike the weary; she struck Sisera, pierced his head, and wounded and penetrated his temple.
At her feet he sank, fell, lay; at her feet he sank fell; where he sank, there he fell down dead.
Through the window the mother of Sisera looked forth, and peered through the window; why is his chariot late in coming? Why tarry the strides of his chariots?
The wisest of her princesses answer her, she too returns answers to herself.

'Are they not finding dividing the spoils? A damsel, two damsels to every man; a spoil of dyed garments to Sisera, a spoil of dyed garments of embroidery; dyed garments of embroidery for the neck of the spoiler.'
So may perish all Your enemies, O Havayah; but they that love Him as the sun when he goes forth in his might." And the land rested forty years.
And the children of Yisroel did that which displeased Havayah, and Havayah delivered them into the hand of Midyan seven years.
And the hand of Midyan prevailed against Yisroel. Because of Midyan the children of Yisroel made for themselves the dens which are in the mountains and the caves, and the strongholds.
And it was, when Yisroel had sown, that Midyan came up, and Amalek, and those of the east; and they came up upon it.
And they encamped against them, and they destroyed the produce of the earth, until you come to Azah. They would leave no sustenance in Yisroel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.
For they and their cattle came up, and their tents, and they came as numerous as locusts; both they and their camels without number, and they came into the land to destroy it.
And Yisroel was very impoverished because of Midyan, and the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah.
Now it was when the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah concerning Midyan,
that Havayah sent a prophet to the children of Yisroel, and he said to them, "Thus Havayah says, Elokim of Yisroel; I brought you up from Mitzrayim, and I brought you out of the house of bondage.
And I saved you from the hand of Mitzrayim, and from the hand of all your oppressors; and I drove them out from before you, and I have given you their land.
And I said to you, 'I am Havayah your Elokim, you shall not fear the deities of the Emorim in whose land you dwell.' But you have not obeyed me."

And the angel of Havayah came, and sat under the oak which was in Ofra, that belonged to Yo'ash the Aviezri; and his son Gidon was beating out wheat in the winepress, to be enabled to flee from Midyan.
And the angel of Havayah appeared and said to him, "Havayah is with you, mighty man of valor."

And Gidon said to him, "Please my master, if Havayah be with us, why then has all this befallen us? And where are all His wonders which our forefathers told us, saying, 'Did not Havayah bring us up from Mitzrayim?' But now Havayah has forsaken us, and He has delivered us into the hand of Midyan."
And Havayah turned toward him and said, "Go, with this your strength, and save Yisroel from the hand of Midyan. Have I not sent you?"
And he said to Him, "Please O Havayah, with what shall I save Yisroel? Behold, my thousand is the poorest in Menasheh, and I am the youngest in my father's household."
And Havayah said to him, "Because I shall be with you, and you shall strike Midyan as one man."
And he said to Him, "If I have now found favor in your eyes, then show me a sign that it is You that speaks with me.
Do not move from here now until I come to you, and I shall bring out my offering, and lay it before you." And he said, "I shall tarry until you return."

And Gidon came and prepared a young goat, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of meal; the meat he put in the basket, and the broth he put in the pot. And he brought it out to him under the oak and presented it.
And the Angel of Elokim said to him, "Take the meat and unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and the broth pour out." And he did so.

And the angel of Havayah put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and he touched the meat and the unleavened cakes. And the fire went up out of the rock, and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes, and the angel of Havayah departed from before his eyes.
Now Gidon saw that he was an angel of Havayah, and Gidon said, "Alas, O Havayah Elokim! Because I have seen the angel of Havayah face to face."
And Havayah said to him, "Peace be to you, fear not, you shall not die."
And Gidon built an altar to Havayah there, and he called it, "Havayah peace." Until this day, it is still in Ofrah of the Aviezrim.

Now it was on that night, that Havayah said to him, "Take the bullock that your father has, and the second bullock, seven years. And you shall destroy the altar of the Baal which belongs to your father, and the Asherah which is next to it shall you cut down.

And you shall build an altar to Havayah your Elokim upon the top of this rock, in the proper place. And you shall take the second bullock, and offer a burnt-offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down."
And Gidon took ten men of his servants, and did as Havayah had spoken to him. Now it was, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city, to do it by day, that he did it at night.

And the men of the city arose early in the morning, and behold, the altar of Baal was broken down, and the Asherah that was next to it, was cut down. And the second bullock was offered upon the altar that was built.
And they said one to another, "Who has done this thing?" And they inquired and sought, and they said, "Gidon the son of Yo'ash has done this thing."
And the men of the city said to Yo'ash, "Bring out your son that he may die, because he has broken the altar of the Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was next to it."

And Yo'ash said to all that stood by him, "Will you contend for the Baal? Will you avenge him? He that will contend for him, shall be put to death; until morning. If he be a deity, let him contend for himself, because he has broken his altar."
And he called him on that day "Yerubbaal," saying, "Let Baal contend with him, because he has broken down his altar."
And all the Midyanim and the Amalekim and those of the east assembled together. And they crossed and encamped in the valley of Yizre'el.
And a spirit of Havayah clothed Gidon, and he blew the trumpet, and Aviezer gathered following him.
And he sent messengers throughout all Menasheh, and they too gathered after him, and he sent messengers to Asher, and to Zevulun, and to Naftali, and they came up towards them.
And Gidon said to Elokim, "If You will save Yisroel by my hand, as You have spoken,

behold, I shall put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there be dew only on the fleece, and upon all the ground it be dry, then I shall know that You will save Yisroel by my hand, as You have spoken."
And it was so, he rose up early on the morrow and pressed the fleece together, and he wrung dew out of the fleece; a bowl full of water.

And Gidon said to Elokim, "Let not Your anger be kindled against me, and I will speak but this once. Let me now experiment but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and on all the ground let there be dew."
And Elokim did so on that night. And it was dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground there was dew.

And Yerubbaal, who is Gidon, arose early, and all the people that were with him, and they encamped beside Ein- harod, and the camp of Midyan was on the north side of him by Givat-Moreh, in the valley.
And Havayah said to Gidon, "The people that are with you are too numerous for Me to give the Midyanim into their hand, lest Yisroel vaunt themselves against Me, saying, 'My own hand has saved me.'

So now proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, 'Whosoever is fearful and trembling, let him return and depart early from Mount Gilad.' " And there returned of the people twenty-two thousand; and ten thousand remained.

And Havayah said to Gidon, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will purify them for you there. And it shall be, that of whom I say to you, 'This shall go with you,' he shall go with you, and of whomsoever I shall say to you, 'This shall not go with you,' he shall not go."

And he brought down the people to the water. Then Havayah said to Gidon, "Everyone who laps with his tongue as the dog laps, him shall you set by himself, and every one that kneels upon his knees to drink."
Now it was the number of those that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, three hundred men, and all the rest of the people kneeled upon their knees to drink water.
And Havayah said to Gidon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and I will give the Midyanim into your hand. Let all the people go each to his place."

And they took the provisions of the people in their hands, and their trumpets; and all the rest of the men of Yisroel he sent each to his tent, but the three hundred men he retained. Now the camp of Midyan was beneath him in the valley.
And it was on that night, that Havayah said to him, "Arise, go down upon the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
But if you fear to go down, go down, you with Purah your lad to the camp.

And you will hear what they speak, and afterward your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down upon the camp." And he went down with Purah his lad to the edge of the armed men that were in the camp.
Now the Midyanim and the Amalekim and all those of the East camped in the valley, as numerous as locusts; their camels without numbers; as numerous as the sand which is upon the seashore.

And Gidon came, and behold, a man was telling his fellow a dream. And he said, "Behold, I dreamed a dream, and behold, a roasted cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midyan, and it came to the tent, and smote it, and it fell; and it turned it upside down, and the tent fell."
And his fellow answered and said, "This is nothing else but the sword of Gidon the son of Yo'ash, the man of Yisroel; Elokim has given Midyan, and all the camp into his hand."

Now when Gidon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down. And he returned to the camp of Yisroel, and said, "Arise, for Havayah has delivered the camp of Midyan into your hands."
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and gave trumpets into the hands of all of them, and empty pitchers with torches inside the pitchers.
And he said to them, "You shall look at me and do likewise. Now behold, when I come to the edge of the camp, then it shall be that as I do, so shall you do.
When I shall blow the trumpet, I and all that are with me, then you too blow the trumpets on every side of all the camp, and say, 'For Havayah and for Gidon.' "

Now Gidon came with the hundred men that were with him to the edge of the camp, in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but recently awakened the guards; and they blew the trumpets, and they smashed the pitchers that were in their hands.

And the three companies blew the trumpets, and broke the pitchers; and they held the torches in their left hands, and in their right hands the trumpets to blow; and they cried, "The sword for Havayah and for Gidon."
And every man stood in his place around the camp; and the entire camp ran, and they trumpeted, and fled.

And they blew the three hundred trumpets, and Havayah set every man's sword against his fellow, and throughout the whole camp. And the camp fled until Bet Hashittah to Zreira as far as the border of Avel-Mecholah, by Tabbat.
And there gathered the men of Yisroel out of Naftali, and of Asher, and of all Menasheh, and they pursued Midyan.

And Gidon sent messengers throughout all the mountain of Efraim, saying, "Come down against Midyan, and seize before them the waters, as far as Beit-barah, and the Yarden." And all the men of Efraim gathered, and they seized the waters as far as Beit- barah, and the Yarden.

And they captured two princes of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev, and they killed Orev at the rock of Orev, and Ze'ev they killed at the winepress of Ze'ev; and they pursued Midyan, and the heads of Orev and Ze'ev they brought to Gidon beyond the Yarden.
And the men of Efraim said to him, "What is this thing that you have done to us; not to call us, when you went to fight with Midyan?" And they quarelled with him vehemently.
And he said to them, "What have I done now in comparison with you? Are not the gleanings of Efraim better than the vintage of Aviezer?
Into your hands has Elokim given the princes of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev; and what was I able to do in comparison with you?" Then their anger was abated toward him, when he said this thing.
And Gidon came to the Yarden; he crossed, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint and pursuing.
And he said to the men of Sukkot, "Give now loaves of bread to the people that follow me, for they are faint, and I am pursuing Zevach and Tzalmunna, the kings of Midyan."
And the officials of Sukkot said, "Is the palm of Zevach and Tzalmunna now in your hand, that we should give your army bread?"
And Gidon said, "Therefore when Havayah delivers Zevach and Tzalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh the thorns of the wilderness and with the briers."
And when he went up from there to Penu'el, and he spoke to them in a like manner; and the men of Penu'el answered him as the men of Sukkot had answered.
And he said also to the men of Penu'el, saying, "When I come back in peace, I will break down this tower."

Now Zevach and Tzalmunna were in Karkor, and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand, all that were left of all the camp of the children of the east; for they that fell were a hundred and twenty thousand men that drew the sword.
And Gidon went up by the way of the tent dwellers on the east of Nobah and Yogbehah, and he smote the camp, for the camp was secure.
And Zevach and Tzalmunna fled; and he pursued after them; and he captured the two kings of Midyan, Zevach and Tzalmunna, and all the camp he terrified.
And Gidon the son of Yo'ash returned from the battle when the sun was still high.
And he caught a youth of the men of Sukkot, and inquired of him: and he wrote down for him the officials of Sukkot, and its elders, seventy-seven men.

And he came to the men of Sukkot, and he said, "Here are Zevach and Tzalmunna whom you did taunt me, saying, 'Is the palm of Zevach and Tzalmunna now in your hand, that we should give to your tired men bread?"
And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and the briers, and with them he broke the men of Sukkot.
And he broke down the tower of Penu'el, and slew the men of the city.
And he said to Zevach and to Tzalmunna, "Where are the men whom you killed at Tavor?" And they said, "As you are, so were they; one was as the form of the children of the king."
And he said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother; as Havayah lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
And he said to Yeter, his first born, "Stand up, kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still young.

Then Zevach and Tzalmunna said, "You stand up and kill us; for as the man is, so is his strength." And Gidon arose, and he killed Zevach and Tzalmunna, and he took the crescents that were on the necks of their camels.
Then the men of Yisroel said to Gidon, "Rule over us, both you, and your son, also your son's son; for you have saved us from the hand of Midyan."
And Gidon said to them, "I shall not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you; Havayah will rule over you."
And Gidon said to them, "I would make a request of you, that you give me, every man, the nose-ring of his spoil." For they had golden nose-rings, because they were Yishmaelim.
And they said, "We shall willingly give." And they spread out the garment, and every man threw therein the nose-ring of his spoil.

And the weight of the golden nose-rings that he requested was one thousand and seven hundred gold, beside the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midyan, and beside the chains that were on the necks of their camels.
And Gidon made it into an Eifod, and he set it up in his city, in Ofrah; and all Yisroel went astray after it there; and it became a snare to Gidon and to his house.
Now Midyan was subdued before the children of Yisroel, and they did not continue to raise their heads. And the land rested forty years in the days of Gidon.
And Yerubbaal the son of Yo'ash went and dwelt in his house.
And Gidon had seventy sons, who came forth from his thigh; for he had many wives.
And his concubine who was in Shechem, she also bore him a son. And he designated his name Avimelech.
And Gidon the son of Yo'ash died in a good old age, and he was buried in the sepulcher of Yo'ash his father, in Ofrah of the Aviezrim.
And it was, when Gidon died, that the children of Yisroel turned again astray after the Be'alim; and they made for themselves Baal-Berit for a deity.
And the children of Yisroel did not remember Havayah their Elokim, who had saved them from the hand of all their enemies around.
And they did not do kindness with the house of Yerubbaal, Gidon, according to all the goodness which he had done to Yisroel.
And Avimelech the son of Yerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother's brothers; and he spoke to them, and to all the family of the house of his mother's father, saying:

"Speak now, in the ears of all the men of Shechem; What is better for you, that there rule over you seventy men, all the sons of Yerubbaal, or that one man rule over you? Now remember that I am your bone and flesh."
And his mother's brothers spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words. And their hearts inclined to follow Avimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
And they gave him seventy pieces of silver of the house of Baal-Berit. And Avimelech hired with them idle and hasty men, and they followed him.
And he went to his father's house, to Ofrah, and killed his brothers, the sons of Yerubbaal, seventy men upon one stone; but Yotam the youngest son of Yerubbaal was left, for he hid.
And all the inhabitants of Shechem and all Beit-Millo assembled, and they went and made Avimelech king, by the plain of stones that was in Shechem.

And they told it to Yotam, and he went and stood on the peak of Mount Gerizim, and he raised his voice, and called; and he said to them, "Listen to me, you men of Shechem, that Elokim may listen to you.
The trees went forth to anoint a king over them. And they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
But the olive tree said to them, 'Should I leave my fatness, wherewith by me they honor Elokim and men, and go to wave over the trees?'
And the trees said to the fig tree, 'Go you, and reign over us.'
But the fig tree said to them, 'Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruitage, and go to wave over the trees?'
And the trees said to the vine, 'Go you and reign over us.'
And the vine said to them, 'Should I leave my wine, which causes Elokim and men to rejoice, and go to wave over the trees? '
Then all the trees said to the thorn, 'Come you, and reign over us.'
And the thorn said to the trees, 'If in truth you anoint me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, let fire come out of the thorn, and consume the cedars of Levanon.'

And now, if you have dealt in truth and with sincerity, in that you have made Avimelech king, and you have dealt well with Yerubbaal and his house, and you have done to him according to the deserts of his hands.
For my father fought for you, and cast his life aside, and saved you from the hand of Midyan.

And you have risen up against my father's house this day, and have killed his sons, seventy men upon one stone, and have made Avimelech, the son of his maid servant, king over the inhabitants of Shechem, because he is your brother.
Now if you have dealt in truth and with sincerity with Yerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice with Avimelech and let him also rejoice with you.

But if not, let fire come out from Avimelech, and consume the inhabitants of Shechem, and Beit-Millo. And let fire come out from the inhabitants of Shechem, and from Beit-Millo, and consume Avimelech."
And Yotam ran away, and fled, and went to Be'er; and he dwelt there because of Avimelech his brother.
And Avimelech ruled over Yisroel three years.
And Elokim sent an evil spirit between Avimelech and the inhabitants of Shechem. And the inhabitants of Shechem betrayed Avimelech.

That might come the injustice done to the seventy sons of Yerubbaal, and their blood to be placed upon Avimelech their brother, who killed them, and upon the inhabitants of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
And the inhabitants of Shechem set for him liers-in-wait on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all that passed by them on the way; and it was told to Avimelech.
And Ga'al the son of Eved came with his brothers, and they entered Shechem, and the inhabitants of Shechem put their trust in him.
And they went out into the field, and gathered their vineyards and trod, and made dances. And they came into the house of their deity, and ate and drank, and cursed Avimelech.

And Ga'al the son of Eved said, "Who is Avimelech and who is Shechem that we should serve him? Is not the son of Yerubbaal? and Zevul his officer? Serve the men of Chamor the father of Shechem, but why should we serve him?
And would that these people were under my hand, then I would remove Avimelech. And he said to Avimelech, "Increase your army, and come out."
And Zevul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Ga'al the son of Eved, and his anger was kindled.
And he sent messengers to Avimelech in secret, saying, "Behold, Ga'al the son of Eved and his brothers are coming to Shechem; and behold, they besiege the city on account of you.
And now, get up at night, you and the people that are with you, and lie in wait in the field.

And it shall be, in the morning, as soon as the sun is shining, you shall rise early, and spread out upon the city; and behold, he and the people that are with him come out against you, then you shall do to him whatever you can."
And Avimelech, and all the people that were with him got up at night, and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
And Ga'al the son of Eved went out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city; and Avimelech and the people that were with him got up from the ambush.
And Ga'al saw the people, and said to Zevul, "Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zevul said to him, "You see the shadow of the mountains as if they were men."
And Ga'al continued to speak, and said, "Behold, people are coming down from the navel of the earth; and one company is coming, by way of the plain Meonenim."
And Zevul said to him, "Where then is your mouth, that you used to say, 'Who is Avimelech that we should serve him?' Is not this the people that you have despised? Go out now, and fight with them."
And Ga'al went out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Avimelech.
And Avimelech pursued him, and he fled before him. And many casualties fell, until the entrance of the gate.
And Avimelech dwelt in Arumah; and Zevul drove out Ga'al and his brothers from dwelling in Shechem.
And it was on the morrow, that the people went out to the field; and they told Avimelech.

And he took the people and divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the field. And he saw, and behold, the people were coming out of the city; and he rose up against them, and struck them.
And Avimelech and the companies that were with him, spread out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city. And the two companies spread out upon all that were in the field, and killed them.
And Avimelech fought against the city all that day; and he captured the city, and killed the people that were therein. And he broke down the city, and sowed it with salt.
And all the inhabitants of the tower of Shechem heard, and they came to the forest of Beit El Brit.
And it was told to Avimelech that all the inhabitants of the tower of Shechem had gathered.

And Avimelech went up to Mount Tzalmon, he and all the people that were with him: and Avimelech took the axes in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, lifted it, and laid it on his shoulder. And he said to the people that were with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry and do like me."

And all the people also cut down every man his bough, and followed Avimelech, and put them nearby the forest, and set the forest on fire upon them; so that also all the men of the tower of Shechem died, about a thousand men and women.
And Avimelech went to Tevetz, and encamped in Tevetz and captured it.
Now there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and the women, and all the inhabitants of the city fled there, and shut themselves in. And they went up to the roof of the tower.
And Avimelech came up to the tower, and fought against it. And he went close to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
And a certain woman cast a piece of an upper millstone upon Avimelech's head, and crushed his skull.
And he called hastily to the young man, his weapon bearer, and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, 'A woman killed him.' " And his young man pierced him, and he died.
Now the men of Yisroel saw that Avimelech had died; and they departed, every man to his place.
Thus Elokim requited the wickedness of Avimelech, which he did to his father, in killing his seventy brothers.
And all the wickedness of the men of Shechem, Elokim requited upon their heads; and there came upon them the curse of Yotam the son of Yerubbaal.
And after Avimelech there arose to save Yisroel, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Yissachar; and he dwelt in Shamir, in the mountain of Efraim.
And he judged Yisroel twenty-three years; and he died, and was buried in Shamir.
And after him arose Yair, the Giladi; and he judged Yisroel twenty-two years.
And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty white colts, and they had thirty cities; they called them "The Villages of Yair" until this day, which are in the land of Gilad.
And Yair died, and was buried in Kamon.

And the children of Yisroel continued to do that which displeased Havayah, and they served the Be'alim, and the Ashtarot, and the deities of Aram, and the deities of Tzidon, and the deities of Moav, and the deities of the children of Amon, and the deities of the Pelishtim. And they forsook Havayah, and did not serve Him.
And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Yisroel, and He delivered them over into the hand of the Pelishtim, and into the hand of the children of Amon.
And they crushed and broke the children of Yisroel that year, eighteen years, all the children of Yisroel that were beyond the Yarden in the land of the Emorim which is in Gilad.
And the children of Amon crossed the Yarden to fight also against Yehudah, and against Binyamin, and against the house of Efraim; and Yisroel was greatly distressed.
And the children of Yisroel cried to Havayah, saying, "We have sinned against You, for we have forsaken our Elokim, and have served the Be'alim."
And Havayah said to the children of Yisroel, "Did not from the Mitzrim, and from the Emorim, from the children of Amon, and from the Pelishtim?
The Tzidonim, and Amalek, and Ma'on oppressed you; and you cried to Me, and I saved you from their hand.
And you have forsaken Me, and have served other deities; therefore I will not continue to save you.
Go and cry to the deities which you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress."
And the children of Yisroel said to Havayah, "We have sinned, do You to us whatsoever pleases you, only deliver us now, this day."
And they removed the strange deities from among them, and they served Havayah: and His soul was grieved by the toil of Yisroel.
And the children of Amon were gathered, and they encamped in Gilad. And the children of Yisroel assembled, and encamped in Mitzpah.
And the people, the princes of Gilad, said each to his friend, "Whosoever shall be the man that will begin to fight against the children of Amon, shall be the head over all the inhabitants of Gilad."
Now Yiftach the Giladi was a mighty man of valor, and he was the son of a woman harlot, and Gilad begot Yiftach.
And Gilad's wife bore him sons; and his wife's sons grew up and drove Yiftach out, and they said to him, "You shall not inherit in our father's house for you are the son of another woman."
And Yiftach fled from his brothers and he dwelt in the land of Tov; and idle men were gathered to Yiftach, and they went out with him.
And it was after many days, and the children of Amon made war with Yisroel.
And it was, when the children of Amon fought with Yisroel; and the elders of Gilad went to take Yiftach from the land of Tov.
And they said to Yiftach, "Come and become our chief, and we will fight with the children of Amon."
And Yiftach said to the elders of Gilad, "Did you not hate me, and drive me from my father's house? So why have you come to me now when you are in distress?"

And the elders of Gilad said to Yiftach, "Therefore we returned to you now, and you shall go with us, and you will fight with the children of Amon, and you shall become our head, over all the inhabitants of Gilad."
And Yiftach said to the elders of Gilad, "If you bring me back to fight with the children of Amon, and Havayah delivers them before me, I will become your head."
And the elders of Gilad said to Yiftach, "Havayah shall hear between us, if not according to your word so will we do."
And Yiftach went with the elders of Gilad, and the people appointed him a head and chief over them; and Yiftach spoke all his words before Havayah in Mitzpah.
And Yiftach sent messengers to the king of the children of Amon, saying, "What is me and you, that you have come to me to fight in my land?"

And the king of the children of Amon said to the messengers of Yiftach, "Because Yisroel took away my land, when they came out of Mitzrayim, from Arnon and up to the Yabbok, and up to the Yarden; and now restore them peacefully."
And Yiftach continued, and sent messengers to the king of the children of Amon.
And he said to him, "So Yiftach said, Yisroel did not take the land of Moav and the land of the children of Amon.
Because when they came up from Mitzrayim, and Yisroel went through the wilderness up to the Yam Suf, and they came to Kadesh.

And Yisroel sent messengers to the king of Edom saying, 'Let me pass now through your land,' and the king of Edom did not listen, and also to the king of Moav he sent, and he was unwilling; and Yisroel abode in Kadesh.

And they went through the wilderness, and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moav, and they came to the east of the land of Moav, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon, and they did not come within the border of Moav, for Arnon the border of Moav.
And Yisroel sent messengers to Sichon, king of the Emorim, the king of Cheshbon; and Yisroel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land up to my place.'
And Sichon did not trust Yisroel to pass through his border, and Sichon gathered all his people, and they encamped in Yahaz, and he fought with Yisroel.
And Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, delivered Sichon and all his people into the hand of Yisroel, and they struck them; and Yisroel possessed all the land of the Emorim, the inhabitants of that land.
And they possessed all the border of the Emorim, from the Arnon up to the Yabbok, and from the wilderness up to the Yarden.
And now Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, has driven out the Emorim from before His people Yisroel, and you want to possess it?
Is it not that which Kemosh your deity gives you to possess, that you may possess; and all that which Havayah our Elokim has driven out from before us, that we shall possess.
And now, are you any better than Balak the son of Tzippor, king of Moav? Did he ever strive with Yisroel, did he ever fight against them?
When Yisroel dwelt in Cheshbon and its towns, and in Aro'er and its towns, and in all the cities that are along Arnon, three hundred years; why did you not recover them at that time?
And I have not sinned against you, and you do wrong with me by fighting against me; may Havayah, the Judge, decide this day between the children of Yisroel and between the children of Amon."
And the king of the children of Amon did not listen to the words of Yiftach which he had sent him.
And a spirit of Havayah was upon Yiftach, and he passed over Gilad and Menasheh, and he passed over Mitzpeh of Gilad, and from Mitzpeh of Gilad he passed over the children of Amon.
And Yiftach vowed a vow to Havayah, and said, "If You will indeed deliver the children of Amon into my hand,

And it will be, whatever comes forth, that shall come forth from the doors of my house towards me, when I return in peace from the children of Amon, shall be to Havayah, and I will offer him up for a burnt-offering."
And Yiftach passed over to the children of Amon to fight against them; and Havayah delivered them into his hand.
And he struck them from Aro'er until you come to Minnit, twenty cities, and up to Hevel Cheramim, a very great slaughter. And the children of Amon were subdued before the children of Yisroel.
And Yiftach came to Mitzpah, to his house, and behold, his daughter was coming out towards him with timbrels and with dances, and she was an only child, he had from her neither a son nor a daughter.

And it was, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have made me fall and you have become one of those that trouble me; and I have opened my mouth to Havayah and I cannot go back."

And she said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to Havayah, do to me according to that which has issued from your mouth, since Havayah has done for you vengeance from your enemies, from the children of Amon."
And she said to her father, "Let this thing be done for me, refrain from me two months, and I shall go, and wail upon the mountains, and I shall cry over my virginity, I and my companions."
And he said, "go," and he sent her away two months; and she went with her companions, and she cried over her virginity upon the mountains.
And it was at the end of two months, that she returned to her father, and he did to her his vow which he had vowed; and she had not known any man, and it was a statute in Yisroel.
From year to year the daughters of Yisroel went to lament the daughter of Yiftach the Giladi, four days in a year.

And the man of Efraim were gathered, and passed to the north; and they said to Yiftach, "Why did you pass to fight against the children of Amon, and you did not call us to go with you? Your house we will burn upon you with fire."
And Yiftach said to them, "I and my people were at great strife with the children of Amon, and I called you, and you did not save me from their hand.

And I saw that you did not save me, and I took my life into my hands, and passed over to the children of Amon, and Havayah delivered them into my hand; so why have you come up to me this day, to fight against me?"

And Yiftach gathered all the men of Gilad, and fought with Efraim; and the men of Gilad struck Efraim, because the lowest of Efraim said, " you Giladim, in the midst of Efraim in the midst of Menasheh."

And the Giladim seized the fords of the Yarden that belonged to Efraim; and it was that when any of the lowest of Efraim said, "Let me go over," and the men of Gilad said to him, "Are you an Efraimi?" and he said, "No."

And they said to him, "Say now 'Shibbolet,' " and he said "Sibbolet," and he was not prepared to pronounce it properly, and they grabbed him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Yarden; and there fell at that time of Efraim, forty-two thousand.
And Yiftach judged Yisroel six years; and Yiftach the Giladi died, and was buried in the cities of Gilad.
And after him Ivtzan of Beit-Lechem judged Yisroel.
And he had thirty sons, and thirty daughters he sent abroad, and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from abroad; and he judged Yisroel seven years.
And Ivtzan died, and he was buried in Beit-Lechem.
And after him Elon the Zevuluni judged Yisroel; and he judged Yisroel ten years.
And Elon the Zevuluni died, and he was buried in Ayalon, in the land of Zevulun.
And after him Avdon the son of Hillel, the Piratoni judged Yisroel.
And he had forty sons and thirty sons' sons, that rode on seventy young donkeys; and he judged Yisroel eight years.
And Avdon the son of Hillel the Piratoni died, and was buried in Piraton, in the land of Efraim, in the mountain of the Amalekim.
And the children of Yisroel continued to do that which displeased Havayah; and Havayah delivered them into the hand of the Pelishtim forty years.
And there was one man from Tzorah, from the family of the Danim, whose name was Manoach; and his wife was barren, and had not borne.
And an angel of Havayah appeared to the woman, and said to her, "Behold now, you are barren, and have not borne; and you shall conceive and bear a son.
Consequently, beware now, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing.

Because you shall conceive, and bear a son; and a razor shall not come upon his head, for a Nazir to Elokim shall the lad be from the womb; and he will begin to save Yisroel from the hand of the Pelishtim."

And the woman came and said to her husband, saying, "A man of Elokim came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of Elokim, very awesome; and I did not ask him from where he was and his name he did not tell me.

And he said to me, 'Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and now do not drink wine and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean, for a Nazir to Elokim shall the lad be, from the womb until the day of his death.' "
And Manoach entreated Havayah, and said, "Please, O Havayah, the man of Elokim whom You sent, let him come now again to us, and teach us what we shall do to the lad that will be born."
And Elokim hearkened to the voice of Manoach; and the angel of Elokim came again to the woman, and she was sitting in the field, and Manoach her husband was not with her.
And the woman hurried and ran, and told to her husband; and she said to him, "Behold, there has appeared to me the man that came to me on that day."
And Manoach arose and went after his wife; and he came to the man, and said to him, "Are you the man that spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."
And Manoach said, "Now your words will come forth; what shall be the rule for the lad, and his doing?"
And the angel of Havayah said to Manoach, "Of all that I said to the woman shall she beware.
From all that comes out of the grapevine she shall not eat, and wine or strong drink she may not drink, and any unclean she may not eat; all that I commanded her, shall she observe."
And Manoach said to the angel of Havayah, "Let us take you in now, and prepare for you a kid goat."

And the angel of Havayah said to Manoach, "If you take me in I will not eat of your bread, and if you will make a burnt-offering, you must offer it to Havayah;" For Manoach did not know that he was an angel of Havayah.
And Manoach said to the angel of Havayah, "What is your name, that when your word will come we may do you honor."
And the angel of Havayah said to him, "Why do you presently ask for my name; since it is hidden."
And Manoach took the kid goat and the meal-offering, and offered it upon the rock to Havayah; and did wondrously, and Manoach and his wife looked on.

And it was, when the flame went up from upon the altar toward heaven, and the angel of Havayah ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoach and his wife looked on, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
And the angel of Havayah did not continue to appear to Manoach and to his wife. Then Manoach knew that he was an angel of Havayah.
And Manoach said to his wife, "We shall surely die, because we have seen Elokim."

But his wife said to him, "If Havayah wanted to kill us, He would not have received from our hand a burnt-offering and a meal-offering, and He would not have shown us all these things; and at this time He would not let us hear as these."
And the woman bore a son and called his name Shimshon; and the lad grew, and Havayah blessed him.
And the spirit of Havayah began to come to him at times in the camp of Dan; between Tzorah and Eshtaol.
And Shimshon went down to Timnah; and he saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Pelishtim.
And he came up, and told his father and mother, and said, "I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Pelishtim; so now take her to me for a wife."

And his father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers and among all my people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Pelishtim?" But Shimshon said to his father, "Take her for me, because she is pleasing in my eyes."
Now his father and mother did not know that it was from Havayah, that he sought a pretense against the Pelishtim; now at that time the Pelishtim were ruling over Yisroel.
And Shimshon and his father and mother went down to Timnah, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah, and behold, a young lion roared towards him.
And there rested on him a spirit of Havayah, and he rent it as one would rent a kid, although he had nothing in his hand, but he did not tell his father and mother what he had done.
And he went down, and he talked concerning the woman, and she was pleasing in Shimshon's eyes.
And he returned after a few days to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, a swarm of bees was in the body of the lion, with honey.

And he separated it into his hands, and he went on, eating as he went, and he went to his father and mother and gave them, and they ate; but he did not tell them that he had separated the honey from the body of the lion.
Now his father went down concerning the woman, and Shimshon made there a feast, because the young men were accustomed to do so.
And it was, when they saw him, that they took thirty companions and they were with him.
Now Shimshon said to them, "Let me ask you a riddle, if you can tell it to me the seven days of feasting and you will guess it, then I will give you thirty linen sheets and thirty suits of clothing.
But if you cannot tell it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen sheets and thirty suits of clothing," and they said to him, "Ask your riddle that we may hear it."
And he said to them, "From the eater came out food, and out of the strong came out sweetness," but they could not tell the riddle for three days.

And it was, on the seventh day, they said to Shimshon's wife, "Persuade your husband, so that he will tell us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire, have you called us here to impoverish us?"

And Shimshon's wife wept upon him, and said, "You only hate me and do not love me; the riddle you have asked my people, but to me you have not told it." And he said to her, "Behold, to my father and mother I have not told it, and to you I shall tell it?"
And she wept upon him the seven days that their feast lasted; and it was, on the seventh day, that he told her, because she had tormented him, and she told the riddle to her people.

And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun set, "What is sweeter than honey and what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "Had you not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle."

And there rested upon him a spirit of Havayah, and he went down to Ashkelon, and killed of them thirty men, and he took their clothing and gave the suits to those who had told the riddle; but his anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house.
And Shimshon's wife was to his companion, who had accompanied him.

And it was, after a few days, in the time of the wheat harvest, and Shimshon remembered his wife with a kid, and said, "I will come to my wife into the room." But her father did not allow him to come in.
And her father said, "I said that you had utterly hated her, and I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her now be yours, instead of her."
And Shimshon said to them, "This time I shall be blameless from the Pelishtim, when I will do them harm."
And Shimshon went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put one torch between two tails in the middle.
And he kindled fire on the torches and set them loose in the standing grain of the Pelishtim, and burnt up from the stacks to the standing grain and to the vineyards and olive trees.

And the Pelishtim said, "Who has done this?" And they said, "Shimshon, the son-in-law of the Timni, because he has taken his wife, and has given her to his companion." And the Pelishtim went up and burnt her and her father with fire.
And Shimshon said to them, "Are you accustomed to do like this? Then I have to be avenged from you and after that I shall cease."
And he struck them, the riders and the foot soldiers, with a great slaughter; and he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
And the Pelishtim went up and encamped in Yehudah; and spread out in Lechi.
And the men of Yehudah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And they said, " to bind Shimshon we have come up; to do to him as he has done to us."

And there went down three thousand men from Yehudah to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and they said to Shimshon, "Did you not know that the Pelishtim rule over us? Now what is this that you have done to us?" And he said to them, "As they did to me, so have I done to them."
And they said to him, "We have come down to bind you, to give you into the hand of the Pelishtim." And Shimshon said to them, "Swear to me, lest you strike me yourselves."
And they spoke to him, saying, "No, however, we will bind you and give you into their hand, but we will not kill you." And they bound him with two new ropes, and brought him up from the rock.

he came up to Lechi, the Pelishtim shouted towards him: and there rested upon him a spirit of Havayah, and the ropes that were upon his arms became as flax that was burnt with fire, and his bonds melted off his hands.
And he found a moist jawbone of a donkey, and put forth his hand and took it, and killed with it a thousand men.
And Shimshon said, "With the jawbone of a donkey I heaped them up; with the jawbone of a donkey I have killed a thousand men."
And it was, when he had finished speaking, that he threw the jawbone from his hand; and called that place Ramat-Lechi.

And he became very thirsty and called out to Havayah and said, "You have given through the hand of Your servant this great deliverance; and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?"

And Elokim cleaved the socket which was in the jawbone, and water came out of it, and he drank, and his spirit returned and he revived; therefore he called its name Ein-Hakkorei, which is in Lechi until this day.
And he judged Yisroel in the days of the Pelishtim twenty years.
And Shimshon went to Azah, and saw there a harlot, and came to her.

To the Azatim saying, "Shimshon has come here," and they compassed and lied in wait for him all night by the gate of the city. And they were quiet the whole night, saying, "Until the morning light and we will kill him."

And Shimshon lay until midnight, and arose at midnight, and laid hold of the doors of the gate of the city, and of the two posts, and he plucked them up together with the bolt and put them upon his shoulders, and he brought them up to the top of the mountain that is facing Chevron.
And it was afterwards, that he loved a woman by the brook of Sorek, and her name was Delilah.

And the lords of the Pelishtim came up to her, and said to her, "Persuade him, and see wherein his strength is so great, and with what we can prevail against him that we may tie him up to torture him: and each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."
And Delilah said to Shimshon, "Tell me now, wherein is your strength so great, and with what you may be tied up to torture you."
And Shimshon said to her, "If I will be bound with seven moist bowstrings that did not dry, then I shall become weak, and be as any man."
And the lords of the Pelishtim brought up to her seven moist bowstrings that did not dry, and she bound him with them.

Now the ambushers stayed in the room, and she said to him, "The Pelishtim upon you Shimshon!" And he tore the bowstrings as a string of tow is torn when it is smelled by fire, and his strength was not known.
And Delilah said to Shimshon, "Behold you have mocked me, and told me lies. Immediately now tell me, with what you may be tied up."
And he said to her, "If I will be tied up with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I shall become weak, and be as any man."
And Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and said to him, "The Pelishtim upon you Shimshon!" and the ambushers were staying in the room. And he tore them from his arms like a thread.
And Delilah said to Shimshon, "Until now you have mocked me, and told me lies, tell me with what you may be tied up." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head to the roller."
And she fastened with the peg, and said to him, "The Pelishtim upon you Shimshon." And he awoke from his sleep, and plucked away the peg of the web and the roller.
And she said to him, "How can you say 'I love you,' while your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me, and you have not told me wherein is your strength so great."
And it was, as she nagged him with her words every day, and pressed him, that his soul was vexed to death.

And he told her all his heart, and said to her, "A razor has not come upon my head, for I am a Nazir to Elokim from my mother's womb. If I will be shaven, then my strength will leave me, and I shall become weak and be like any man."

And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called the lords of the Pelishtim saying, "Come up this time, for he has told me all his heart." And the lords of the Pelishtim came up to her, and brought the money in their hands.
And she put him to sleep upon her knees, and she called the man, and she shaved off the seven locks of his head. And she began to afflict him, and his strength left him.

And she said, "The Pelishtim upon you Shimshon!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times, and I will shake myself," but he did not know that Havayah had departed from him.
And the Pelishtim seized him, and gouged out his eyes. And they brought him down to Azah, and bound him with copper chains, and he did grind in the prison house.
And the hair of his head began to grow after he was shaven.
And the lords of the Pelishtim gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their deity and to rejoice. And they said, "Our deity has delivered our enemy Shimshon into our hands."
And the people saw him and praised their deity, because they said, "Our deity has delivered into our hands our enemy and the destroyer of our land, and who has slain many of us."

And it was when their hearts were merry, that they said, "Call for Shimshon, and he will make sport for us." And they called for Shimshon out of the prison-house, and he made sport before them, and they stood him between the pillars.
And Shimshon said to the lad that held him by his hand, "Allow me, and let me feel the pillars whereupon the house rests, that I may lean upon them."
Now the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Pelishtim were there. And upon the roof about three thousand men and women, the spectators of Shimshon's sport.

And Shimshon called out to Havayah and said, "O Havayah Elokim, remember me and strengthen me now, only this once O Elokim, that I may be avenged the vengeance for one of my two eyes from the Pelishtim."
And Shimshon grasped the two pillars of the center, upon which the house rested, and leaned upon them, one with his right hand and the other with his left.

And Shimshon said, "Let my soul die with the Pelishtim," and he bent with might, and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein. And the dead that he killed at his death were more than he had killed in his lifetime.

And his brothers and all his father's household came down, and carried him, and brought him up and buried him between Tzorah and Eshtaol in the burying place of Manoach his father. And he judged Yisroel twenty years.
Now there was a man from the mountain of Efraim, and his name was Michayahu.

And he said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, and you did curse, and you also spoke in my ears. Behold the silver is with me, I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son to Havayah."

And he restored the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, "I have dedicated the silver before Havayah from my hand for my son to make a graven image and a molten one, and now I will restore it to you."

And he restored the money to his mother. And his mother took two hundred pieces of silver, and gave them to the founder, and he made thereof a graven image and a molten one, and it was in the house of Michayahu.
Now the man Michah had a house of idolatry. And he made an ephod and teraphim, and initiated one of his sons, who became his priest.
In those days no king in Yisroel; every man did what was right in his eyes.
And there was a lad from Beit-Lechem in Yehudah, of the family of Yehudah, and he was a Levi, and he sojourned there.
And the man went out of the city, out of Beit-Lechem in Yehudah, to sojourn where he could find. And he came to the mountain of Efraim, to the house of Michah, to make his way.
And Michah said to him, "From where do you come?" And he said to him "I am a Levi from Beit-Lechem in Yehudah, and I go to sojourn where I may find."

And Michah said to him, "Dwell with me, and be to me an instructor and a priest, and I will give you ten pieces of silver for the period, and a wardrobe of clothing with your provisions." And the Levi followed.
And the Levi was content to dwell with the man. And the lad was to him as one of his sons.
And Michah initiated the Levi, and the lad became his priest, and was in the house of Michah.
And Michah said, "Now I know that Havayah will be good to me, because I had a Levi as my priest."

In those days no king in Yisroel; and in those days the tribe of the Danim sought for themselves an inheritance to dwell, for until that day there had not fallen to them among the tribes of Yisroel an inheritance.

And the children of Dan sent from their families five men, part of them men of valor, from Tzorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to search it; and they said to them, "Go search the land." And they came to the mountain of Efraim, up to Michah's house, and lodged there.

they by the house of Michah, they recognized the voice of the lad, the Levi. And they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? And what have you here?"
And he said to them, "Such and such has Michah done for me, and he has hired me, and I have become his priest."
And they said to him, "Ask now of Elokim, that we may know whether we shall be prosperous on our way upon which we are going."
And the priest said to them, "Go in peace; before Havayah is the way in which you shall go."

And the five men went, and arrived in Layish. And they saw the people that were therein dwelling in security, after the manner of the Tzidonim, tranquil and secure; for there was none in the land to put them to shame for any thing; heirs being few, and they were far from the Tzidonim, and had no bond with any man.
And they came to their brothers, Tzorah and Eshtaol; and their brothers said to them, "What do you?"
And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good; and you are silent, do not be lazy to go and enter to possess the land.

When you arrive, you will come to a secure people, and the land is sufficiently large, for Elokim has given it into your hands; a place where there is nothing lacking of anything which is in the land."
And there journeyed from there, of the Dani family, out of Tzorah and Eshtaol, six hundred men girded with weapons.
And they went up and encamped near Kiryat-Ye'arim, in Yehudah; therefore they called that place "The camp of Dan" until this day; behold behind Kiryat-Ye'arim.
And they passed from there to the mountain of Efraim, and came up to Michah's house.

And the five men that went to spy out the area of Layish spoke up, and said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod, teraphim, a graven image, and a molten one? And now know what you have to do."
And they turned there, and came to the house of the young man the Levi, in Michah's house, and greeted him.
Now the six hundred men of the children of Dan girded with their weapons, stood by the entrance of the gate.

And the five men that went to spy out the land went up; they came in there, took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. And the priest stood by the entrance of the gate with six hundred men that were girded with weapons.
And these came into Michah's house, and took the graven image with the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. And the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

And they said to him, "Be still, put your hand over your mouth and go with us, and be to us an instructor and a priest. Is it better for you to be a priest to the house of one man, or to be a priest to a tribe and family in Yisroel?"
And the priest was pleased, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image, and he came in the midst of the people.
And they turned and departed, and put the little ones, the cattle, and the goods before them.
They were at a distance from the house of Michah, when the men that were in the houses which were near Michah's house were gathered, and they overtook the children of Dan.
And they called the children of Dan, and they turned their faces. And they said to Michah, "What is with you, that you are gathered?"
And he said, "My deity which I made you took away, in addition to the priest, and you have gone away. What else have I? How then can you say to me, 'What is with you?' "
And the children of Dan said to him, "Let not your voice be heard among us, lest men of embittered souls assail you, and you will lose your life, and the lives of your household."
And the children of Dan went their way. And Michah saw that they were stronger than he, and he turned and went back to his house.

And they took that which Michah had made, and the priest whom he had; and they came to Layish, to a people tranquil and secure, and they struck them with the edge of the sword. And the city they burnt with fire.
And there was no one to save, because it was far from Tzidon, and they had no bond with any man, and it was in the valley that lies by Beit-Rechov. And they built the city and dwelt therein.
And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Yisroel, but actually Layish was the name of the city at first.

And the children of Dan set up for themselves the graven image. And Yehonatan the son of Gershom, the son of Menasheh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danim until the day of the exile of the land.
