And they accepted for themselves the graven image of Michah which he had made, throughout the period that the house of Elokim was in Shilo.
And it was in those days, when there was no king in Yisroel, that there was a Levi man dwelling by the edge of the mountain of Efraim, who took for himself a concubine from Beit- lehem to Yehudah.
And his concubine turned away from him, and went from him to her father's house, to Beit-Lechem of Yehudah. And she was there for a period, four months.

And her husband arose and went after her, to persuade her to return, and his servant was with him, and a team of donkeys. And she brought him into her father's house, and the father of the girl saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
And his father-in-law, the girl's father, kept him, and he abode with him for three days. And they ate and drank and lodged there.

And it was on the fourth day, that they arose early in the morning, and he rose up to depart. And the girl's father said to his son-in-law, "Refresh yourself with a morsel of bread, and afterward you shall depart."
And they sat down and both of them ate together, and they drank. And the girl's father said to the man, "Accept now and lodge, and let your heart be content."
And the man rose up to depart; but his father-in-law urged him, and he returned and lodged there.
And he arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart, and the girl's father said, "Refresh yourselves now," and they tarried until the day declined, and they both ate.

And the man rose up to depart, he, his concubine, and his servant. And his father-in-law, the girl's father, said to him, "Behold, now the day has weakened to set, lodge now, behold it is the resting of the day, lodge here, and your heart will be content, and you will arise early for your way, and go to your dwelling place."
But the man did not want to lodge, and he arose and departed, and came over against Yevus, which was Yerushalayim. And with him was a team of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
They were near Yevus as the sun descended very much; and the servant said to his master, "Come now, and let us turn aside to this city of the Yevusim and lodge in it."
And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside into city of heathens, that are not of the children of Yisroel, but we will journey up to Givah."
And he said to his servant, "Come and let us approach to one of these places; and we will lodge in Givah or in Ramoh."
And they passed on and went. And the sun set upon them near Givah which belonged to Binyamin.
And they turned aside there to come and lodge in Givah. And he came and sat in the thoroughfare of the city, but no one brought them home to lodge.
And behold, an old man came from his work out of the field at evening, and the man was from the mountain of Efraim, and he resided in Givah; but the people of the area were Binyaminim.
And he raised his eyes, and saw the wayfaring man in the thoroughfare of the city; and the old man said, "Where are you going and from where do you come?"

And he said to him, "We are passing from Beit-Lechem of Yehudah to the edge of the mountain of Efraim, from there am I, and I went until Beit-Lechem of Yehudah; and I am going to the House of Havayah, and no one takes me home.
And also there is straw and provender for our donkeys, and also bread and wine for myself, for your maidservant, and for the lad who is with your servants; there is no want of anything."
And the old man said, "Peace be to you, just let all your needs be upon me, but do not lodge in the street."
And he brought him into his house, and gave fodder to the donkeys, and they washed their feet, ate and drank.

As they were enjoying themselves, and behold, the men of the city, men of wickedness, surrounded the house, beating at the door. And they spoke to the man, the elderly master of the house, saying, "Bring out the man that came into your house, so that we may be intimate with him."
And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brothers, do not do so wickedly now. Since this man has come into my house, do not commit this disgraceful deed.
Here is my virgin daughter, and his concubine, I will bring them out now and afflict them, and do with them as you please, but to this man do not do this disgraceful act."

But the men did not want to listen to him, and the man grabbed his concubine, and brought her forth to them outside. And they were intimate with her, and abused her the entire night until the morning, and they sent her away when the day began to dawn.
And the woman came as the morning began. And she fell down at the entrance of the man's house, where her master was, until it was light.

And her master arose in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way. And behold, the woman, his concubine, was lying after having fallen at the entrance of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
And he said to her, "Arise, and let us go," but no one answered. And he took her upon the donkey, and the man rose up and went to his place.
And he came to his house, and took the knife, and took hold of his concubine and cut her into limbs, into twelve pieces, and he sent her throughout all the borders of Yisroel.

And it came to pass anyone that saw, would say, "There has not happened nor has there been seen like this from the day that the children of Yisroel came up from the land of Mitzrayim until this day; concern yourself about it, take counsel, and speak."
And all the children of Yisroel went out, and the congregation was assembled as one man, from Dan to Be'er Sheva, and the land of Gilad, to Havayah, to Mitzpah.
And there presented themselves the chiefs of all the people, of all the tribes of Yisroel, in the assembly of the people of Elokim, four hundred thousand footmen that drew the sword.
And the children of Binyamin heard that the children of Yisroel had gone up to Mitzpah. And the children of Yisroel said, "Speak, how has this wickedness come about?"
And the Levi man, the husband of the murdered woman answered and said, "I came into Givah that belongs to Binyamin, I and my concubine to lodge.
And the residents of Givah arose against me, and surrounded the house upon me at night. Me they intended to kill, and my concubine they afflicted, she died.
So I grabbed my concubine and dissected her and sent her throughout the territory of the inheritance of Yisroel; for they committed lewdness and disgrace in Yisroel.
Behold, you are all children of Yisroel, give yourselves a decision and advice here."
And all the people arose as one man saying, "No man will go to his tent and no man will turn to his house.
And now this is the thing which we will do to Givah; against it by lot.

And we will take ten men of a hundred, from all the tribes of Yisroel, and a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to take provisions for the people, that they may do when they come to Givah of Binyamin, according to all the disgrace that was done in Yisroel."
And all the men of Yisroel were gathered concerning the city, as one man in unison.
And the tribes of Yisroel sent men throughout all the tribes of Binyamin saying, "What wickedness is this that has come about among you?

Therefore now deliver the wicked men that are in Givah and we will put them to death, and we will remove evil from Yisroel." But the children of Binyamin did not want to obey their brothers, the children of Yisroel.
And the children of Binyamin were gathered out of the cities to Givah, to go out to battle against the children of Yisroel.
And the children of Binyamin numbered on that day, out of the cities twenty-six thousand men that drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Givah, who numbered seven hundred chosen men.
Of all these people there were seven hundred chosen men shriveled right hand. All these could sling a stone at a hair-breadth and not miss.
And the men of Yisroel numbered, excluding Binyamin, four hundred thousand men that drew the sword, all these were men of war.

And they arose and went up to Beit-El, and asked of Elokim, whereupon the children of Yisroel said, "Who shall go up for us first to battle against the children of Binyamin?" And Havayah said, "Yehudah first."
And the children of Yisroel rose up in the morning, and they encamped against Givah.
And the men of Yisroel went out to battle against Binyamin. And the men of Yisroel arrayed battle against them at Givah.
And the children of Binyamin came out of Givah, and they destroyed of the Bnei Yisroel on that day twenty-two thousand men, to the ground.
And the people, the men of Yisroel, encouraged themselves, and set again in array the battle in the place where they set themselves in array on the first day.

And the children of Yisroel went up, and wept before Havayah until the evening, and they asked of Havayah saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the children of Binyamin my brother?" And Havayah said, "Go up against him,"
And the children of Yisroel approached the children of Binyamin on the second day.
And Binyamin went out towards them from Givah on the second day, and destroyed of the children of Yisroel another eighteen thousand men to the ground; all these were swordsmen.

And all the children of Yisroel went up, and all the people, and they came to Beit-El and wept, and sat there before Havayah, and fasted on that day until the evening. And they offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Havayah.
And the children of Yisroel asked of Havayah, for there was the ark of the covenant of Elokim in those days.

And Pinchas the son of Elazar the son of Aharon stood before it in those days saying, "Shall I again go out to battle with the children of Binyamin my brother, or shall I cease?" And Havayah said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand."
And Yisroel set liers-in-wait against Givah around.
And the children of Yisroel went up against the children of Binyamin on the third day, and set themselves in array against Givah, as at the previous times.

And the children of Binyamin went out towards the people, until they were drawn away from the city; and they began to kill of the people casualties as previously, along the highways, of which one goes up to Beit-El, and the other to Givah, in the field thirty men of Yisroel.
And the children of Binyamin said, "they are beaten before us, as at first," but the children of Yisroel said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."
And all the men of Yisroel rose up out of their place, and set themselves in array at Baal-Tamar. And the liers-in-wait of Yisroel drew forth out of their place, out of Ma'areh-Geva.
And there came over against Givah ten thousand chosen men of all Yisroel, but the battle was heavy, because they did not know that misfortune was approaching them.
And Havayah beat Binyamin before Yisroel, and the children of Yisroel destroyed of Binyamin on that day twenty-five thousand and one hundred men; all of these were swordsmen.
And the children of Binyamin saw that they were beaten, and the men of Yisroel gave place to Binyamin, because they trusted in the liers-in-wait that they had set against Givah.
And the liers-in-wait hastened, and scattered upon Givah. And the liers-in-wait blew, and smote the entire city with the edge of the sword.
Now there was an appointed time between the men of Yisroel and the liers-in-wait, that they should make a great pillar of smoke rise from the city.
Now as the men of Yisroel turned in battle, Binyamin began to kill, casualties of the men of Yisroel thirty men, for they said, "Surely they are beaten before us, as in the previous battle."
And the pillar began to rise from the city, a column of smoke, and the Binyaminim turned behind themselves, and behold, there arose the entire city towards heaven.
And the men of Yisroel turned, and the men of Binyamin panicked, for they saw that misfortune was approaching them.
And they turned from before the men of Yisroel towards the way of the wilderness, but the the war caught up with them; and of the cities destroyed them within it.
They encircled the Binyaminim, they called a pursuit upon them, resting places they overtook them, as far as against Givah, along east.
And there fell of Binyamin eighteen thousand men, all these men of valor.

And they turned and fled to the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and they gleaned of them in the highways five thousand men; then they pursued after them until Gidom, and killed of them two thousand men.
Now it was all that fell of Binyamin twenty-five thousand swordsmen on that day; all these men of valor.
And they turned and fled to the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, six hundred men; and they abode in the rock of Rimmon four months.

And the men of Yisroel turned upon the children of Binyamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, from the city even the cattle, even all that was found. Also, all the cities which they found they set on fire.
Now the men of Yisroel had sworn in Mitzpah, saying, "No man from us shall give his daughter to Binyamin for a wife."
And the people came to Beit-El, and sat there until the evening before Elokim, and raised their voices and wept profusely.
And they said, "Why O Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, has this come to pass in Yisroel, that one tribe of Yisroel should be missing today?"
And it was on the next day that the people rose early, and built there an altar, and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings.

And the children of Yisroel said, "Who is there among all the tribes of Yisroel that did not come up to Havayah in the assembly?" for there was a great oath concerning him that did not come up to Havayah at Mitzpah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."
And the children of Yisroel reconsidered concerning Binyamin their brother, and said, "Today, one tribe has been cut off from Yisroel.
What shall we do for them that remain, for wives, since we have sworn by Havayah not to give them of our daughters for wives?"
And they said, "Which one of the tribes of Yisroel did not go up to Havayah at Mitzpah?" and behold, no one had come to the camp from Yavesh-Gilad to the assembly.
And the people were counted, and behold, no one was there of the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilad.

And the congregation sent there twelve thousand of the valiant men, and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilad with the edge of the sword, including the women and the children.
And this is the thing that you shall do; every male, and every woman that had relations with man you shall destroy."
And they found among the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilad four hundred virgin girls that had not had relations with any man; and they brought them to the camp, to Shilo which is in the land of Kena'an.
And the whole congregation sent and spoke to the children of Binyamin that were in the rock of Rimmon, and they proclaimed to them peace.
And Binyamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had saved alive of the women of Yavesh-Gilad; but this was not sufficient for them.
And the people reconsidered concerning Binyamin, because Havayah had made a breach in the tribes of Yisroel.
And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for those that remained for wives, since the women of Binyamin have been destroyed?"
And they said, " an inheritance for the remnant of Binyamin, so that a tribe not be blotted out from Yisroel.
But we may not give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Yisroel have sworn, saying, 'Cursed that gives a wife to Binyamin.' "

And they said, "Behold, there is a sacrifice before Havayah in Shilo from time to time, which is to the north of Beit-El, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Beit-El to Shechem, and to the south of Lebonah."
And they instructed the children of Binyamin, saying, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.

And you will see, and behold, if the daughters of Shilo come out to dance in the dances, then you shall come out of the vineyards and you shall grab for yourselves each man his wife of the daughters of Shilo, and go to the land of Binyamin.

And it shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to quarrel with us, then we will say to them, 'We took pity on them, because we did not take for each man his wife in the war, for you did not give them presently that you should be guilty.' "

And the children of Binyamin did so, and married wives according to their numbers, of those that danced whom they had seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance, and built the cities and dwelt in them.
And the children of Yisroel went from there at that time, every man to his tribe and family, and they departed from there every man to his inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Yisroel; every man did what was right in his eyes.
